title: Evolutionary Database Design
core_concepts: schema plus data in version control
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: represent every change as a small, version-controlled migration applied by a tool that tracks applied changes. RECOMMENDED: a private database per developer and at least daily integration. Small changes are easier to get right and errors are quicker to find.
practical_examples: Rename a table and keep a view under the old name during the transition phase; a CI server applies migrations to its own database copy and runs the full build.
why_it_matters: Sets the baseline lifecycle for schema change that the rest of the framework refines.
authority_rationale: Written by the originators of the practice and published on a widely recognized engineering site.
notes: Does not present stored procedures as a general encapsulation layer; recommends a clearly separated data access layer.

title: ParallelChange
engineering_principles: MANDATORY for incompatible changes under continuous delivery: support old and new versions together, move clients incrementally, then remove the old version. The cost is maintaining two versions and needing discipline to finish.
practical_examples: Most database refactorings follow this pattern; the migrate phase is the transition between the original and new schema.
why_it_matters: Provides the single meta-pattern from which safe DDL sequences can be derived.
authority_rationale: Canonical definition of the pattern on a recognized engineering site.
notes: Credits Joshua Kerievsky with first documenting the technique in 2006.

title: Refactoring Databases: Evolutionary Database Design
organization_author: Scott W. Ambler and Pramod J. Sadalage (Addison-Wesley Professional)
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: make small changes that improve design without changing semantics, and support old and new schemas in parallel so application teams can deploy on their own schedule.
practical_examples: Catalog chapters cover structural, data quality, referential integrity, architectural and method refactorings, plus transformations; the companion site is databaserefactoring.com.
why_it_matters: Gives the framework a named vocabulary of schema change types.
authority_rationale: Foundational book by originating authors in the Fowler Signature Series.
notes: Only the publisher page was read, not the book text. ISBN-13 978-0-321-29353-4.

title: Migration Style Guide
engineering_principles: MANDATORY at GitLab: no migration may require downtime. Time limits are 3 minutes for regular migrations, 10 minutes for post-deployment migrations and 20 minutes for concurrent index creation; single background migration queries stay under 1 second with cold caches.
practical_examples: with_lock_retries for high-traffic tables, disable_ddl_transaction! for concurrent indexes, add_concurrent_index, explicit index names, bigint for large counters and timezone-aware timestamps.
why_it_matters: Supplies concrete, enforceable budgets and helpers for a schema change policy.
authority_rationale: Internal engineering standard from a major organization operating a large PostgreSQL deployment.
notes: Rules are specific to GitLab's Rails and PostgreSQL stack. Examples reference milestones up to 18.10.

title: Avoiding downtime in migrations
engineering_principles: MANDATORY at GitLab: spread incompatible changes over several releases so running code never sees a missing structure. Ignoring and dropping a column must not happen in the same release.
practical_examples: ignore_column then remove_column in a post-deployment migration then remove the rule; rename_column_concurrently; change_column_type_concurrently; drop each foreign key before dropping a table.
why_it_matters: Directly supplies safe sequences for the framework's dangerous-operations table.
authority_rationale: Major-organization engineering standard grounded in production operation.
notes: This page defers foreign key and NOT NULL details to separate guides. The NOT NULL guide is cited in the markdown notes.

title: Online migrations at scale
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: migrate in four phases (dual write, change reads, change writes, remove old data), keeping both stores consistent at every step and verifying in production.
practical_examples: Migrated hundreds of millions of Subscriptions objects; backfilled offline from database snapshots with Hadoop and Scalding, then reran the job to confirm nothing was missed.
why_it_matters: Shows how to verify a large data migration without heavy production queries.
authority_rationale: Major-organization engineering blog describing a real production migration.
notes: The article gives no exact record count.

title: Braintree PostgreSQL safe operations redux (gist blog.md)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY at Braintree: hold exclusive locks for about 2 seconds at most, keep code and schema forward- and backward-compatible, and do not revert schema on rollback. A waiting lock queues all later queries on the table.
practical_examples: Add a CHECK constraint NOT VALID then validate instead of a direct NOT NULL; add foreign keys NOT VALID; retry lock acquisition after pausing and checking for long-running queries.
why_it_matters: Explains the lock mechanics behind most PostgreSQL migration incidents.
authority_rationale: Practitioner write-up of a high-volume payments operator's rules.
notes: The page has no formal title; title here is descriptive. Covers PostgreSQL 9.1 to 12, so check rules against current versions. The original 2014 post is at https://pgrs.net/2014/05/14/safe-operations-for-high-volume-postgresql/. The Medium/PayPal URL in the brief returned HTTP 403.

title: strong_migrations README
engineering_principles: MANDATORY per the README: set a short lock timeout for migrations. Other checks fail by default and offer an expand-and-contract or concurrent alternative; raw SQL cannot be verified by the tool.
practical_examples: lock_timeout of 10 seconds and statement_timeout of 1 hour; set timeouts with ALTER ROLE under PgBouncer transaction mode; add foreign keys with validate: false then validate separately.
why_it_matters: A ready-made list of operations an automated gate should flag across PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB.
authority_rationale: Widely known tool documentation by a well-known practitioner.
notes: Page shows no release version; footer 2026.

title: ALTER TABLE (PostgreSQL 18 documentation)
engineering_principles: Authoritative facts: non-volatile defaults need no rewrite, volatile defaults and most type changes rewrite the table and indexes, validation takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, and a valid CHECK constraint lets SET NOT NULL skip its scan.
practical_examples: ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY ... NOT VALID followed by VALIDATE CONSTRAINT.
why_it_matters: Ground truth for classifying PostgreSQL operations as safe or dangerous, by engine version.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY behaviour is on a separate page cited in the markdown notes. Rewriting forms are not MVCC-safe.

title: Versioned migrations (Flyway documentation)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: migrations apply in order exactly once, and an applied migration is not edited once it reaches a permanent downstream environment; add a new migration and roll forward.
practical_examples: File V001.002__NewTwitterColumn.sql; Flyway Desktop adds a timestamp by default to reduce version conflicts between team members.
why_it_matters: Defines the immutable, ordered migration history model.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of a leading migration tool.
notes: Undo caveats (Teams edition; assumes the whole migration succeeded) are at https://documentation.red-gate.com/fd/undo-migrations-273973334.html. The page does not state what happens on a checksum mismatch.

title: Using Liquibase Rollback
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: test rollback scripts like application code using a deploy, roll back, redeploy cycle. Structural changes combined with data migration are harder to roll back.
practical_examples: update-testing-rollback in CI; future-rollback-sql so auditors can confirm every change has a rollback.
why_it_matters: Represents the pro-rollback position in the down-migration controversy.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of a leading migration tool.
notes: Some commands are Liquibase Secure only. Automatic rollback coverage is at https://docs.liquibase.com/workflows/liquibase-community/automatic-custom-rollbacks.html.

title: Auto Generating Migrations (Alembic documentation)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: manually review and correct every candidate migration, since autogenerate is not intended to be perfect. Name constraints explicitly so they can be tracked.
practical_examples: Table and column renames appear as add and drop pairs and must be hand-edited into a rename.
why_it_matters: Evidence for requiring human review of ORM-generated DDL.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of the standard SQLAlchemy migration tool.
notes: CHECK constraint detection is name-based only and off by default.

title: Atlas migration lint analyzers
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: analyze migration files in CI against coded rule families for destructive, data-dependent, incompatible, blocking and naming violations.
practical_examples: DS102 table dropped, MF104 nullable to non-nullable, BC102 column rename, PG101 missing CONCURRENTLY, NM101 to NM106 naming conventions.
why_it_matters: A rule taxonomy the framework's automated validator can adopt.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of a reputable schema tool.
notes: Many PostgreSQL and MySQL analyzers require Atlas Pro. Declarative vs versioned concepts are at https://atlasgo.io/concepts/declarative-vs-versioned.

title: Introduction to DevOps Database Delivery
engineering_principles: OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL: neither approach is ideal. State-based deployment scripts do not understand the data context of a change, while migration-based scripts accumulate and must run in order.
practical_examples: A state-based table rename drops and recreates the table without preserving data unless extra scripts are written; a team may start state-based and move to migrations once the database stabilizes.
why_it_matters: Frames the main authoring trade-off for the framework.
authority_rationale: Vendor practitioner article; the vendor sells tools for both approaches.
notes: Replaces the Redgate approaches page, which now only states SQL Change Automation is retired from sale.

title: Database change management (DORA capability)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: keep changes as scripts in version control, apply them with tooling and test them on a production-like, scrubbed data set. The stated goal is 100% of database changes through a fully automated process.
practical_examples: Measure the share of failed changes involving the database, added lead time, downtime cost and the automated share of changes.
why_it_matters: Links database practice to delivery performance and supplies metrics.
authority_rationale: Summary from a major research program; the page itself is guidance rather than a peer-reviewed paper.
notes: resource_type is the closest enum value; this is a capability summary. Accelerate (2018) was not opened.

title: Squawk Rules Overview
engineering_principles: RECOMMENDED: lint PostgreSQL migrations in CI for statements that could block reads or writes.
practical_examples: Rules include require-concurrent-index-creation, constraint-missing-not-valid, prefer-bigint-over-int, prefer-timestamptz, ban-drop-column and renaming-column.
why_it_matters: Low-cost automated gate for the dangerous operations list, plus type checks.
authority_rationale: Official documentation of a specialist open-source linter.
notes: The overview page lists rule names only; descriptions are on individual rule pages not opened.

title: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems
engineering_principles: MANDATORY for federal systems and used here as the reference vocabulary: derive MTD, RTO and RPO from the BIA, keep RTO shorter than MTD, test backups regularly and store encryption keys separately from backups.
practical_examples: Offsite vendor criteria cover geographic area, accessibility, security, environment and cost; alternate sites are cold, warm, hot, mobile or mirrored.
why_it_matters: Provides the formal definitions for recovery objectives.
authority_rationale: Published by a national standards body.
notes: A US federal guideline; international_standard is the closest enum value. Text was extracted locally from the downloaded PDF. Landing page: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/34/r1/upd1/final.

title: Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery (PostgreSQL 18 documentation)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: set up and test WAL archiving before the first base backup, and design archive commands to refuse overwriting existing files. Monitor archiving and consider keeping several backup sets.
practical_examples: archive_mode on with archive_command; pg_basebackup; restore_command with recovery.signal and a time or named restore point target.
why_it_matters: Shows that RPO depends on continuous log archiving, not only on backup frequency.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: pg_dump cannot be part of a continuous-archiving solution. Configuration files are not restored.

title: Back up and Restore of SQL Server Databases
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: testing is required; a backup strategy does not exist until backups are restored in every planned combination and checked for physical consistency. Store backups separately, encrypt them and use least privilege.
practical_examples: Restore to a test system and run DBCC CHECKDB; use BACKUP CHECKSUM and RESTORE VERIFYONLY; document procedures in a run book.
why_it_matters: Strongest vendor statement of the restore-testing rule.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: Warns that restoring a .bak file from an untrusted source can compromise the instance.

title: Oracle Database 19c Backup and Recovery User's Guide: Introduction
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: physical backups are the foundation; logical backups supplement them but are not sufficient alone. RMAN is the preferred tool.
practical_examples: Use Oracle Flashback Table to return tables to an earlier time without taking the database offline; Flashback Database requires a fast recovery area.
why_it_matters: Clear vendor position in the logical versus physical backup debate.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: Data Guard is covered on a separate page cited in the markdown notes.

title: Disaster recovery options in the cloud (AWS whitepaper)
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: test backups and keep point-in-time backups alongside replication, since replication may not protect against corruption or malicious deletion. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL: choose the tier by RTO, RPO and cost.
practical_examples: Copy backups across accounts and Regions with AWS Backup; schedule periodic automated restores; redeploy infrastructure with IaC.
why_it_matters: Gives the DR tier model and explicit support for the rule that replication is not backup.
authority_rationale: Official vendor whitepaper.
notes: RPO and RTO ranges per tier were in a figure and were not captured.

title: #StopRansomware Guide
engineering_principles: MANDATORY: keep offline, encrypted backups of critical data and regularly test their availability and integrity, because many ransomware variants seek out and delete or encrypt accessible backups.
practical_examples: Maintain golden images and version-controlled IaC templates offline; restore from offline backups in order of critical services.
why_it_matters: Adds the attacker model that reachable backups are not safe backups.
authority_rationale: Joint guidance from US government security agencies.
notes: Does not mention the 3-2-1 rule or specify backup retention periods; 3-2-1 is sourced in the markdown notes from the CISA Data Backup Options PDF.
